title: Tool Definitions and Function Calling
summary: Tool calling lets a model request actions in a structured way: you describe functions as schemas, the model emits a call, your code runs it and returns the result as more context. This lesson covers the schema, the loop, what the definitions cost, and how reliability multiplies down a chain of calls.
objectives: Write a tool definition as a JSON Schema and explain what the model actually sees
Trace the tool-call loop and compute its token cost and latency over several rounds
Estimate how tool count affects the cost of definitions and the chance of choosing the right tool
Compute end-to-end success for a chain of calls from selection and argument accuracy, and the effect of validate-and-retry
Treat tool results as untrusted context and keep them small and well-formed
prerequisites: You should understand structured outputs and JSON Schema from [Few-Shot Examples and Structured Outputs](/learn/prompt-and-context/few-shot-and-structured) and the idea of a growing prompt from [Anatomy of a Prompt](/learn/prompt-and-context/prompt-anatomy). Agents, which build whole systems from this loop, come in module 7.
